title: Evaluation of Preoperative Anxiety in Digestive Surgery
official: Evaluation of Preoperative Anxiety in Digestive Surgery
summary: This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the association between preoperative anxiety and postoperative complications in patients undergoing major oncological digestive surgery. The study will assess whether preoperative anxiety is associated with the occurrence of major postoperative complications at 90 days, measured using the Comprehensive Complication Index (CCI).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older
* French-speaking patients
* Patients scheduled to undergo major oncological digestive surgery at the Digestive Surgery Department of Rouen University Hospital
* American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status classification ≤3
* Patients who have read and understood the study information letter and have not objected to participation in the study
* Patients affiliated with a social security system

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindication to surgery
* Long-term use of anxiolytic, hypnotic and/or antidepressant medication
* Previous psychiatric or psychological disorder likely to prevent the participant from understanding the study requirements or from providing valid non-opposition to participation
* Pregnant, parturient or breastfeeding women
* Persons deprived of liberty by administrative or judicial decision
* Persons under judicial protection, including safeguard of justice, guardianship or curatorship
